## Same-cycle factual repair

The public/search review exposed a real site-owned chronology defect. `/product/`, `/architecture/`, and `/pricing/` used fixed historical review dates while interpolating the **current** `site.version` and `productCommit`. After the 5 September release sync this rendered impossible statements such as “Reviewed on 24 August 2026 against AgentSight v1.0.31” even though v1.0.31 did not exist until 5 September. Code search confirmed the same pattern on all three source sections.

This defect takes priority over speculative content work. The smallest coherent repair is limited to those three source sections:

- re-read the three pages against the current v1.0.31 product source and release change;
- verify product PR `#209` changed fleet/frontend loading and mobile/session usability while explicitly leaving authentication, capability, organization, and backend policy unchanged;
- verify the current v1.0.31 Controller still exposes the documented Free/Pro/Team/Enterprise catalog and `HOSTED_PREVIEW_UNLIMITED` behavior;
- replace the impossible “Reviewed on [old date] against current version” construction with a truthful split: **last substantively reviewed on 7 September 2026**, while the linked primary sources resolve against the site's current AgentSight release/version/commit.

The wording intentionally separates editorial review time from the dynamically current source target. A future release can move `site.version`/`productCommit` without silently rewriting the historical review date into a claim that the older review examined a release that did not yet exist.

### Search-facing change boundary

- Evidence: current public Product output plus repository code showed the impossible date/version pairing after the v1.0.31 release.
- Affected routes: `/product/`, `/architecture/`, `/pricing/`, source-review paragraphs only.
- Preserved behavior: all page headings, product claims, pricing values, navigation, routes, canonical tags, metadata, structured content outside the source-review wording, analytics, sitemap, and unrelated pages.
- Representative unaffected routes: `/`, `/blog/how-agentsight-loads-agent-fleets-progressively/`, `/security/`.
- Expected effect: remove false chronology while keeping exact current-release source links discoverable.
- Public acceptance: each affected route must show `Last substantively reviewed on 7 September 2026` and current AgentSight v1.0.31 / `bb99b66f...` source identity; the old impossible review sentences must be absent; representative unaffected pages and canonical metadata must remain unchanged.
- Rollback point: cycle-start `main` commit `4de2d7c993d391d05ca06da553a30748b0309559`.

This narrow factual repair is not a qualifying substantive technical publication, so it does **not** reset the 48-hour content clock. The deadline remains 8 September 09:53:06 PDT.
